status_note: Preliminary: derived from very few real calls; timing parameters are point estimates with no meaningful confidence interval.
clock_resolution_note: The real run measured with time.monotonic() on Windows, which ticks at about 15.6 ms; values such as 0.0, 15.0/16.0 and 47.0 ms are quantised to that grid, so stream durations below ~16 ms are not resolvable. The API now uses time.perf_counter().

estimators.first_content_median_ms: geometric mean of pooled samples (lognormal median estimate)
estimators.completion_tokens: median provider-reported completion tokens (includes hidden reasoning tokens; content is synthetic)

assumptions: Distribution shape: lognormal per stage; sigma values (0.6 first-content, 0.5 stream) are synthetic, not estimated (n <= 3 per stage cannot support a spread estimate).
Pooling: draft and draft_expanded are pooled because the stand-in sees only the prompt; their real latency may differ with prompt length.
The first draft sample (2078.0 ms) is more than 3x the others ([468.0]); the cause (connection setup, cold start, provider variance) was not measured and all samples are kept.
The first interpret sample (2671.0 ms) is more than 3x the others ([531.0]); the cause (connection setup, cold start, provider variance) was not measured and all samples are kept.
Long tail (probability, multiplier) is synthetic: no tail was observed in 6 calls.
Load slowdown with concurrency is synthetic: the real run was sequential (no concurrent calls measured).
Error, 429 and malformed-stream rates are synthetic: none were observed.
Prompt-token usage reported by the stand-in is chars/4 (synthetic); completion tokens use the calibrated per-stage median.
Minute/day limit enforcement semantics (sliding 60 s minute window, calendar simulated-UTC day) are synthetic; only the limit values in header_advertised_limits were observed.
Real Groq replenishes request/token budgets on a rolling basis (reset headers); the stand-in day window resets at simulated UTC midnight.
